title: Faith in Christ or the Faithfulness of Christ?
lead: The Greek phrase pistis Christou (or pistis Iesou Christou), found in Galatians 2:16, 20; 3:22, 26 (compare Romans 3:22, 26 and Philippians 3:9), can mean 'faith in Christ' (Christ as the object of faith: the objective genitive) or 'the faith, or faithfulness, of Christ' (Christ as the one who is faithful: the subjective genitive). The question has divided translators and commentators since the 1980s, and it changes how Paul's account of justification reads.

sections.b: For 'faith in Christ': most English versions; the stress in Galatians 2:16 on 'we believed in Christ Jesus'; Paul's use of the verb 'believe' with Christ as object; Luther, Calvin, and recent defenders such as Dunn, Moo, Fitzmyer and Schreiner. For 'the faithfulness of Christ': the ordinary sense of the genitive in many similar phrases (faith of Abraham, Romans 4:12, 16); the avoidance of redundancy (justified through faith in Christ so that we believe in Christ); and the story of Christ's obedient death (Philippians 2:8); defenders include Hays, Wright in part, Campbell, Longenecker and Martyn. Greek grammar alone does not settle it.
sections.refs: Galatians 2:16; Galatians 2:20; Galatians 3:22; Galatians 3:26; Romans 3:22; Romans 3:26; Philippians 3:9
